title: Smoothness at a point is invariant under smooth source maps
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Smoothness is tested on compatible etale scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. An open subspace is a subfunctor whose pullback along every scheme-valued object is an open subscheme. Let $h:X\to Y$ and $q:Z\to X$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $B$, with $q$ smooth. A point of a space is a field-valued section modulo isomorphism and common field extension; its topology is detected by etale scheme charts. For every $z\in|Z|$, $h\circ q$ is smooth at $z$ if and only if $h$ is smooth at $q(z)$. Smooth at a point means smooth on some open neighbourhood of that point. No surjectivity assumption on $q$, and no flatness or local finite presentation assumption on $h$, is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06F2, lemma-smooth-smooth-local-source, with definition-property-morphisms-local-source. Pointwise form: restrict q to a smooth neighbourhood and its open image, then use smooth-source descent; composition is spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03ZD (lemma-composition-smooth), and openness of the image is spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 042S (lemma-fppf-open) with Tag 04TA (lemma-smooth-flat).

proof.text: Open subspace inclusions are representable etale: every scheme pullback is an open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). They are therefore smooth by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Algebraic spaces may be viewed as discrete algebraic stacks: sheaf descent supplies their stack condition and their etale scheme atlases are smooth. Their maps are representable by algebraic spaces by the same calculus node. The two conventions for a property $P$ among smooth, flat and locally of finite presentation agree for a map $f:G\to F$ of spaces. $P$ is etale local on source-and-target by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], and the chart notion of the statement is the one of [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion]. If $f$ has $P$ as a representable map, choose etale scheme atlases $V\to F$ and $U\to G\times_FV$. Criterion (1) for $G\times_FV\to V$ gives $P(U\to V)$, and $U\to G$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and composition, so criterion (2) gives $P$ for $f$ on charts. Conversely, if $f$ is smooth on charts, every scheme base change $G\times_FT\to T$ is smooth by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality], so $f$ is smooth as a representable map. Suppose $h$ is smooth at $q(z)$, and choose an open subspace $A\subseteq X$ containing $q(z)$ with $h|_A$ smooth. The open pullback $Z_A=Z\times_XA$ contains $z$, by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. Its projection to $A$ is smooth by base change of $q$. Its composite to $Y$ is smooth by composition, so $hq$ is smooth at $z$.

source.place: Tags 03ZE (lemma-base-change-smooth), 03ZD (lemma-composition-smooth), 04XX (lemma-etale-smooth); morphisms.tex Tag 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale); spaces-properties.tex Tag 03IE (lemma-factor-through-open-subspace).; stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XC (lemma-property-spaces-too) and spaces-descent.tex Tag 0429 (lemma-descending-property-smooth) for the agreement of the chart and representable conventions.

proof.text: Conversely, choose an open subspace $W\subseteq Z$ containing $z$ on which $hq$ is smooth. The map $q_W:W\to X$ is smooth by step 1 and composition. Thus it is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], on charts by the comparison of step 1. By [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open] its point image is open in $|X|$. The open-subset correspondence in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] gives an open subspace $O\subseteq X$ with $|O|=\operatorname{im}|q_W|$. By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], $q_W$ factors uniquely as $r:W\to O\hookrightarrow X$, and $W\times_XO\to W$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $r$ is the base change of $q_W$ along $O\hookrightarrow X$, so is smooth. It is surjective on point classes by the choice of $O$. Put $g=h|_O$; then $gr=(hq)|_W$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 06F2 (lemma-smooth-smooth-local-source), pointwise reduction; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 04TA (lemma-smooth-flat), 04AJ (lemma-smooth-locally-finite-presentation), 042S (lemma-fppf-open); spaces-properties.tex Tags 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces), 03IE (lemma-factor-through-open-subspace).

proof.text: We now perform the chart argument for $g$, rather than assuming a smooth-source descent theorem for spaces. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $b:V\to Y$ and a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to O\times_YV$. Their composite $a:U\to O$ is surjective etale by base change and composition of etale covers [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers, lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Write $d:U\to V$ for the other map. Form $E=W\times_OU$, an algebraic space by the fibre-product node, and choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $T\to E$. The resulting $p:T\to U$ is smooth and surjective: $E\to U$ is the base change of the smooth point-surjection $r$, and the atlas is smooth and surjective. Base change and composition preserve these properties by the fibred-groupoid calculus. Since $p$ is a map of schemes, it is smooth on charts by the comparison of step 1, hence smooth in the scheme sense by the scheme clause of [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion]. The other composite $c:T\to W$ is etale, because $E\to W$ is the etale base change of $a$. From $bd=ga$ and $r\circ(E\to W)=a\circ(E\to U)$ we get $b\circ(dp)=g\circ a\circ p=(gr)\circ c$.

source.place: Tag 06ER (lemma-transfer-from-schemes), proof: choose V, U, and a scheme atlas of the pullback of the source cover; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target); descent.tex Tag 04R3 (remark-list-local-source-target), smooth entry.

proof.text: Scheme smoothness is etale local on source-and-target by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] to the smooth map $gr:W\to Y$ and the presentation diagram $(c:T\to W,b:V\to Y,dp:T\to V)$: it gives smoothness of $dp$. The smooth scheme morphism $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation as a representable map by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], hence in the scheme sense by the comparison of step 1 and the scheme clause of the criterion, and is surjective by step 3. Thus [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] applied to $T\xrightarrow{p}U\xrightarrow{d}V$ gives smoothness of $d$, with no finite-presentation hypothesis on $d$ in advance. The presentation $(a:U\to O,b:V\to Y,d)$ has $a$ surjective etale, so the presentation criterion gives smoothness of $g:O\to Y$.

source.place: Tag 06ER (lemma-transfer-from-schemes), the three equivalences, specialized to smoothness as in Tag 06F2; descent.tex Tag 05B5 (lemma-smooth-permanence), smooth case, supplies the scheme source-descent implication.

proof.text: Since $z\in|W|$, its image $q(z)$ lies in $|O|$. Step 4 proves that $h$ restricted to this open neighbourhood is smooth, so $h$ is smooth at $q(z)$. Together with step 1 this is the equivalence claimed. If $Z$ is empty there are no points to test; otherwise the argument for each $z$ makes $W$ and $O$ nonempty. The image $O$ may be a proper open of $X$, so no surjectivity of the original $q$ is needed. No flatness or local finite presentation of $h$ was assumed.
